text:
lina: Quick note — saw a small regression when bringing pelican-v0.9 through int8: JP->ZH chrF -0.03 concentrated on lines mixing Han + Arabic fragments and varied punctuation.
raj: Can you paste a minimal repro and tokenizer outputs?
lina: Sure, short example and token dumps: 
```
Source: 

FP16 tokens: ["北","\u4eac","\u00b7","\u0627","\u062c","\u0644","\u0627","\u2014","\u30c6"]
INT8 tokens: ["北","\u4eac","\u30fb","\u0627","\u062c","\u0644","\u0627","-","\u30c6"]
```
(Notice U+00B7 vs U+30FB and U+2014 vs hyphen)
marc: That looks like input normalizer differences; we trim vocab during int8 bringup which also updated the tokenizer artifact build. Could be canonicalization mismatch.
raj: Simple mitigation — canonicalize punctuation to NFKC and map common mid-dots/dashes before tokenization. Example patch: 
```
s = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', s)
s = s.replace('\u00B7', '\u30FB')
s = s.replace('\u2014', '-')
```
Put behind tokenize.canonicalize_punct flag.
lina: Ran that locally — tokens align and mini-bench chrF recovers ~0.028. Good candidate fix.
ci-bot: smoke-run pelican-v0.9-int8 4942000138: chrF_base=0.610, chrF_int8_canary=0.606 (canary=5% traffic), regression_count_down_by=89%
marc: Plan: PR for canonicalizer + unit tests with tricky fixtures, canary rollout on int8 pools. If regressions remain we'll audit tokenizer artifact trimming.
lina: Assigned: raj canonicalizer PR, marc tests & canary, lina follow-up metrics. Will update when CI completes.
